title: Reduce capacity-planner coupling and fast-path node recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over time the capacity planner and node lifecycle code have accumulated implicit coupling: provisioning heuristics, scoring signals, and transient lease handling are intertwined. This causes long tail reconciliation pauses, brittle upgrades, and repeated race conditions during node recovery (OOM, preemptions). Goal: Separate decision graph concerns from actuator side-effects and provide a thin, deterministic fast-path for node recovery events so user-visible capacity and request latency impact is minimized. Scope: refactor capacity-planner core to expose a pure decision API, extract legacy heuristic plugins behind feature flags, implement a lightweight node-recovery handler that can short-circuit slow planner paths, and add end-to-end tests + dashboards. Out of scope: full move to event-sourcing or major datastore migration (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Capacity planner exposes a stable decision API used by autoscaler and node-recovery handler
Fast-path node recovery reduces tail reconciliation time for preempted GPUs from median 12s to <=3s in test harness
No increase in allocation churn or failed bindings observed in integration smoke runs
New unit/integration tests cover heuristic plugin behavior and emergency fast-path
Rollout controlled by feature flag with automatic fallback and monitoring alerts
plan: Spike (2d): map current planner decision graph, record call-sites that mutate cluster state (Aisha)
Design (3d): spec DecisionAPI and fast-path contract; circulate to runtime and infra (Marco)
Implementation (8d): extract pure planner core, add plugin adapter layer, implement fast-path handler behind FF (pair: Marco + Elena)
Tests (4d): unit tests for DecisionAPI, integration harness for preemption/full-recovery scenarios (CI job)
Canary (3d): enable on non-prod pool, monitor reconciliation latency and allocation success rates
Rollout (2d): progressive enablement across pools with health gates and rollback via FF
